description: A warren run dispatched to pi+openrouter (moonshotai/kimi-k3) died mid-task with failureReason=provider_error ('Provider finish_reason: error') at ~52k context after five cached turns, having written src/forge/contract.ts and src/forge/fake/ but committed NOTHING. All 16 minutes and $1.19 were lost: the run branch on origin pointed at main's commit, and salvage had nothing to rescue because there were no commits in the workspace. A retry of the identical issue with one added instruction — 'git commit incrementally as each part lands rather than saving one commit for the end' — survived past the same context window and produced 9 commits, which is exactly what let warren's salvage path recover the complete tree when a SECOND, unrelated infrastructure failure hit (warren-5202). The lesson is not about the model: uncommitted agent work is invisible to every warren recovery mechanism. Salvage can only rescue what is committed.
resolution: Put an explicit incremental-commit instruction in every dogfood dispatch prompt: commit after each discrete part lands, not once at the end. Pair it with context economy (targeted greps over full-file reads, no throwaway python/sed bulk-rewrite scripts) for long single-PR steps. Both together turned a total loss into a full recovery on the same issue.

name: plan-step-body-is-the-spec
description: When a dogfood dispatch prompt is built from a seeds plan child, the seeds row is often NOT the spec. For plan pl-d1c9 every child's description contains only a seeds:plan-backref comment; the real specification lives in the plan step body, reachable as: sd plan show <pl-id> --json | jq -r '.plan.sections.steps[<plan_step_index>].description' where plan_step_index comes from sd show <id> --json. A prompt telling the agent only to run 'sd show <id> --json' hands it a backref and nothing else. Separately, plan step bodies written before phase 1 merged had drifted from HEAD: warren-0fac's body told the agent to implement a cross-fork PR search fix that already shipped in PR #824 (src/runs/pr.ts:172-195), and warren-1fe0's body asserted both new check:layers rules were 'born green' when four live non-test modules still violated the import twin. Reading a plan step as authoritative without re-verifying against HEAD produces prompts that ask agents to redo or regress shipped work.

A git rebase of a local .seeds/issues.jsonl commit onto origin/main SILENTLY DROPPED three newly-created issues (warren-c042, warren-5202, warren-fe9b) and a description addendum on a fourth (warren-0fac), resolving the conflicted file to main's version. The dangerous part is that every standard integrity signal passed: git reported the path as UU but the file contained ZERO conflict markers, 'jq -r .id .seeds/issues.jsonl | sort | uniq -d' printed nothing, and 'bun run check:seeds-integrity' would have reported ok — because the result was internally consistent, just missing rows. The documented seeds hazard (warren-9c90 / warren-db8c) is the merge=union DUPLICATE-row shape, and the runbook check (uniq -d) only detects that shape. This is the inverse failure — lost rows, not duplicated ones — and it is invisible to that check. Detected only by explicitly asserting that each expected id was present after the rebase. warren-0fac additionally showed the split-truth shape: main's row had the correct blockedBy (null, since warren-1fe0 had closed) while the local row had the correct description (the dispatch addendum); taking either row wholesale would have lost one of them.
resolution: After ANY rebase or merge touching .seeds/issues.jsonl, do not stop at 'uniq -d is empty' and 'check:seeds-integrity ok'. Explicitly assert every id you created or edited this session is still present, e.g. for id in <ids>; do jq -r --arg i $id 'select(.id==$i)|.id' .seeds/issues.jsonl; done — a missing id prints nothing. Recover dropped rows from the pre-rebase commit with 'git show <sha>:.seeds/issues.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.id==...)'' and append. For a row both sides edited, merge field-wise: take blockedBy from the side that removed a blocker (intersect) and the description from the side that added content, rather than taking either row whole.

description: CORRECTION to the earlier 'incremental commits saved the work' record: the instruction is an unreliable mitigation with moonshotai/kimi-k3, not a fix. Across seven pl-d1c9 dispatches carrying an explicit 'git commit incrementally as each part lands, do not defer your first commit' instruction, three runs (warren-45e6, warren-63e7, warren-0b49) went 20-35 minutes and 90-130k context with ZERO commits before their first one. warren-45e6 sat at 131k context with nothing committed — the same total-loss exposure that cost run 1 of warren-1fe0 sixteen minutes and $1.19 when OpenRouter returned finish_reason: error. The instruction demonstrably helped some runs and was ignored by others; the runs that did commit early were not obviously different in task shape. Compounding it: there is NO mid-run correction channel. POST /runs/:id/steer is a documented silent no-op for the pi agent (warren-3305) — the steer is accepted, recorded as steer.sent, and never delivered to the harness. So an operator watching a run accumulate uncommitted work at 130k context can do nothing but wait.
resolution: Keep the incremental-commit instruction — it costs nothing and helps sometimes — but do NOT treat it as protection. Plan dogfood sessions on the assumption that any run can lose everything up to its first commit. Concretely: prefer smaller-scoped issues over large single-PR steps where the model may work 30+ minutes before committing, and treat a run sitting past ~20 minutes with zero commits as a known-exposed window rather than something you can intervene in. Fixing warren-3305 (pi steering delivery) would convert this from unfixable to recoverable, which is the higher-leverage change.

name: ratchet-the-allowlist-per-step
description: A migration campaign that lands its enforcement gate BEFORE its consumers are migrated can still be born green, and can drive its own exemptions to zero, if each step is told to delete the allow-list entries its own work frees. pl-d1c9's check:layers forbidImports rule shipped in warren-1fe0 with a five-entry allow list (the seam itself plus four pre-migration consumers), each entry carrying a why that NAMED the later step which deletes it. Then: warren-45e6 removed src/runs/pr.ts and pr-annotate.ts, warren-63e7 removed src/runs/pr-checks.ts, warren-0b49 removed src/ci-fixer/check-runs.ts. Final state is  alone — the seam fully enforced with zero exemptions, reached without anyone auditing it manually at the end. Two things made it work: the why field on each entry told the next agent which entry was ITS responsibility, and every dispatch prompt restated the current list plus 'delete yours, the list only shrinks'. Without the restatement an agent has no reason to look at the file at all, since its migration passes the gate either way — a stale entry silently re-permits a violation forever.

name: verify-agent-scope-narrowing
description: When a dispatched agent reports that it did LESS than its spec said, verify the claim against HEAD rather than accepting or overriding it — twice in pl-d1c9 the agent was right and the plan was wrong. (1) warren-6c4c's step body named nine token fan-out call sites; the agent migrated seven and reported that plan-runs.ts cancel and runs/pause-resume.ts were not per-spawn git credentials. Reading both at HEAD confirmed it: each spreads deps.autoOpenPr into a cancel path performing an INLINE REAP that opens a PR over REST, so forge.gitCredential was the wrong boundary. They belonged to warren-45e6. (2) warren-2600's falsification test could not register a fake:// project because src/projects/url.ts was GitHub-specific; the agent checked forge-contract §0's domain list, found src/projects/ absent, and extended the seam rather than special-casing the fake. Both reports were load-bearing scope decisions that would have been invisible in a summary. The prompt line that produced them: 'if you find a tenth, say so explicitly in your report rather than silently fixing or skipping it' and 'if you must edit domain code to make this pass, STOP and report — that falsifies the claim and is more valuable as a finding than as a silent fix.'

warren-c80e's bucket-3 inventory (~15 domain files importing burrow types) was stale on its own write date: the 2026-07-16/17 burrow-client eviction had already cleared it, and check:layers enforces the end state. Caught by the good-first-issue-batch HEAD-verification pass before publishing it as contributor work (2026-08-13 GFC batch GH#846-849). Lesson: multi-bucket seeds rot per-bucket — verify each bucket against HEAD independently before planning or publishing from the seed.
resolution: Amended warren-c80e's description and ROADMAP items 2/4 with the verified state; dropped the dead bucket from the GFC batch; published only the four HEAD-verified issues

description: merge-seeds-jsonl driver on an 'unresolvable' conflict (warren-5f0d updatedAt false positive) leaves OURS content in the working .seeds/issues.jsonl — committing it blindly resurrects the other side's closes (warren-fb2d briefly read open while closed on main during PR #859 repair).
resolution: Never trust the driver's working-file output after a nonzero exit. Rebuild from the merge stages: git show :2/:3, id-keyed jq merge with closed-wins, blockedBy-intersect, updatedAt-max; verify with jq dup check + check:seeds-integrity before committing. Filed warren-585f.

name: serial-schema-plan-dispatch-repair-cadence
description: Serial schema-heavy plan through the dogfood pipeline (pl-103e, 13 children, 2026-08-14): dispatch next child on previous-terminal, expect EVERY schema child's PR to go DIRTY on migration journal slots + .seeds, and dispatch a repair run immediately (repairs overlap the sequential loop). Repair prompt must say: keep main's migrations, delete own generated files, regenerate with db:generate; .seeds closed-wins/blockedBy-intersect; budgets take main. Session totals: 13 issue runs + 10 repair runs + 1 manual merge (24 runs), ~$35.7, ~7h wall clock, zero lost closes, zero failed runs on kimi-k3/pi. Only the first and last PRs of the chain merged without a repair.

Bun auto-loads the cwd .env into process.env, so any warren CLI invocation from the repo root silently uses the repo's stale WARREN_API_TOKEN (env outranks the login config file AND piped stdin): login --token reports success while every later command 401s. Diagnose by comparing 'resolveClientConfig token prefix' vs the file; the giveaway is flag-mode working while file/stdin modes fail.
resolution: Run warren with explicit WARREN_BASE_URL/WARREN_API_TOKEN per command (wrapper script in scratchpad), or run from a cwd without a .env. Tracked: warren-8807/GH#898 (doctor hint), warren-2244 (login source warning).

name: serial-tech-debt-dispatch-slice
description: Tech-debt dogfood slice 2026-08-16: 23 seeds issues dispatched serially to pi+openrouter/kimi-k3 on app.warren.run; 23/23 runs succeeded, 23 PRs (#900-#920,#922,#923) + 1 repair run, ~$13.6 total (~$0.55/issue, median run 10-20min). Working pattern: per-issue prompt = sd show first + merged-main context + scope guardrails + 'check:all is terminal' + sd close instruction; same-file issues strictly ordered behind their predecessor's MERGE (not just terminal run), independent issues interleaved into the gap; gh pr update-branch after every upstream merge keeps the serial auto-merge chase cheap. Sole CI failure was a contract collision (scenario 39 expected the old 501 the issue's fix deliberately removed) — repair run on the PR branch updated the scenario, correct outcome.

name: cli-env-token-source-naming
description: CLI auth footgun fix: Bun auto-loads cwd .env so ambient WARREN_API_TOKEN wins silently — login prefers piped stdin over env, and commandFailure names the env token source on 401/403

PR #928 opened DIRTY while touching .seeds/.mulch; the seeds-merge-autoheal pull_request-opened run never healed it, likely because GitHub reported mergeable=UNKNOWN when the event fired and the workflow early-exited as not-CONFLICTING. The warren-c84c push-to-main trigger does not cover born-conflicted PRs.
resolution: Manual driver-aware merge in a throwaway worktree (git merge origin/main with the seeds-jsonl driver registered, verify check:seeds-integrity + dup-id scan, push). Filed warren-c97b for an opened-event mergeability retry.

name: auto-merge-rearm-on-synchronize
description: Validated live repeatedly (PRs #928, #931, #941, #942...): after the warren-4681 fix (#926), any push to an eligible open PR (heal merge, update-branch) triggers the auto-merge gate to re-evaluate and arm. Manual gh pr merge --auto is no longer needed on non-Article-IX PRs; the shepherding loop reduces to update-branch chasing.

content: Acceptance scenario 39 (public-instance leak guard, the only CI-wired scenario) asserts Vary: Authorization on every route so shared caches cannot serve an operator body to a spectator. When adding any route, set the header via the shared response helper, and check scripts/acceptance/scenarios/39-public-exposure.ts for per-route expectations (cache-control, CSP) before opening the PR.

name: concurrent-pipeline-territory-contracts
description: This session ran the tech-debt queue while a second agent ran the burrow-absorption plan (pl-3007) in the same repo. What worked: explicit file-territory declaration up front, merge-gated sequencing across pipelines (peer held src/runtime/k8s/ until my fe9b+d15c and 32f8 merged, signalled by SendMessage pings), queue reordering to cut peer idle (~3h→~1h by promoting 32f8), and a shared .seeds conflict doctrine (closed wins, INTERSECT blockedBy, check:seeds-integrity). Cross-pipeline conflicts still happened twice (src/plan-runs/retry.ts #938, src/runtime/local/provider.ts #948) and were fixed by repair runs — acceptable price; do not try to serialize whole pipelines.

PR #959 (warren-ea0a, burrow excision) rewrote scripts/check-layers.ts in the same window PR #957 (warren-d382) replaced it with the module-graph implementation. Git's auto-merge on the #959 branch silently took the ea0a side — the d382 rewrite would have been reverted on merge with no textual conflict. Caught only because CI failed on the merge ref. This is the guard-script variant of the seeds-jsonl problem: id-keyed data has a driver, whole-file rewrites have nothing.
resolution: Peer restored the module-graph implementation + tests from main and ported its burrow-rule test fixtures onto surviving seams. Doctrine adopted for concurrent pipelines: when both pipelines touch the same guard script, whoever merges second must explicitly diff their branch's copy against the version landed on main (git diff origin/main -- <file>) before merging, not trust a clean auto-merge.
